verdict.rationale: dlt is fundamentally code/API-first: the CLI can create, inspect, and deploy pipelines (dlt-docs-10), the Python API covers pipeline runs and dataset queries (dlt-docs-12, dlt-docs-29), and the dltHub MCP server exposes inspection, debugging, secrets, schema and run management (dlt-docs-47, dlt-docs-72) mirroring what the Web UI (app.dlthub.com) offers for monitoring (dlt-docs-15). A community user directly corroborates this, stating 'I can do everything via code' when comparing dlt to a UI tool built atop it (dlt-comm-9). Missing for 10: no explicit vendor statement enumerating full UI-vs-API parity or any documented case of a UI-only feature, so full symmetry is inferred rather than exhaustively confirmed.
